reveal_en: The English word "muscle" derives from the Latin "musculus," which literally translates to "little mouse." Ancient Romans observed contracting muscles, particularly the biceps, and saw a resemblance to mice scurrying under the skin.
reveal_zh: 英语“muscle”一词源自拉丁语“musculus”，意为“小老鼠”。古罗马人观察到肌肉收缩，尤其是二头肌，形似皮肤下窜动的老鼠。
meaning_en: This reveals the poetic and often surprising origins of everyday language, rooted in ancient observations of the human body.
meaning_zh: 这揭示了日常词汇背后充满诗意且常出人意料的起源，根植于古人对人体的观察。

visual.motion: A flexing bicep, with a faint, almost illusory "mouse-like" movement beneath the surface.
